name: blob-card
title: Blob Card
description: A dark pricing card for a Pro plan at $99, whose header is a pool of blurred pink blobs that drift and chase the cursor. A slow conic glow runs around the card edge, with a CTA and a feature list below.
use: A pricing or product card should feel premium and alive without extra imagery or stock photos.
avoid: The pink palette is hardcoded and large blurred layers are costly, so it fights a neutral brand and weak devices.
a11y: The animated blob and glow layers are not marked aria-hidden and ignore reduced-motion, so they keep pulsing for everyone. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A tall rounded card on black with a magenta-pink header of soft blurred blobs holding Pro, an early-supporter tag and a big $99 beside a struck $149. A white Get Instant Access button sits above five icon-and-text features and a small footer line.
behaves: The blobs drift on their own and lean toward the pointer when it enters the header, while a conic glow slowly rotates around the card border. Blob size and opacity keep pulsing; the text and button stay still.
customise: Pass header and children nodes, plus headerHeight, light, dark and glow colour arrays and className. The blob physics and glow timing are in the source.
weight: moderate: Four blurred blobs and a rotating conic glow animate every frame; blur is the main cost.
demo: Pro plan at $99 (was $149), one-time, with five features like all premium components and direct support.
issues: The rotating glow border is so faint it is easy to miss against the dark stage.
Feature icons and light grey body text are low contrast on the dark card.
polishWhy: Premium bottled-blob header and a tidy feature list; faint body text and a barely visible glow.
